# ui::testing::TestSpellChecker

Header: `winui/testing/TestSpellChecker.hpp`.

Derives from `ui::SpellChecker`.

Deterministic, in-process [SpellChecker](../rendering/spell-checker.md) for headless tests. It uses no system dictionary, only the words the test declared misspelled.

Every change (a new misspelling, a settings flip, add/ignore/autocorrect) bumps [generation()](#generation), which tells a synced control to check again. Always reports "en-US" while available. Words are runs of letters, digits, underscores and apostrophes, matched with exact case.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::testing::HeadlessTextMeasurer measurer;
ui::TextBoxControl tb{"Ths is a tset"};
const ui::Size size = tb.measure({200.0f, ui::Unbounded}, measurer, ui::Theme::default_light());
tb.arrange({100.0f, 100.0f, 200.0f, size.height});
ui::testing::set_focused(tb, true);

ui::testing::TestSpellChecker checker;
checker.add_misspelling("Ths", {"This"});
checker.add_misspelling("tset", {"test"});
tb.sync_spell_checker(checker);
tb.tick(ui::Duration{0}); // checking happens on the next tick, never inside the sync

REQUIRE(tb.spelling_errors().size() == 2);
REQUIRE(checker.check_count() == 1);
REQUIRE(checker.suggest("Ths") == std::vector<std::string>{"This"});
```

## add_misspelling

```cpp
void add_misspelling(std::string word, std::vector<std::string> suggestions = {})
```

Declares `word` (exact case) misspelled, with the list [suggest()](#suggest) returns for it.

## set_available

```cpp
void set_available(bool available)
```

Simulates a missing or present system dictionary. While unavailable, checks find nothing and [language()](#language) is empty. Default true.

## set_highlight_enabled

```cpp
void set_highlight_enabled(bool enabled)
```

Flips the user's "highlight misspelled words" setting (default true).

## set_autocorrect_enabled

```cpp
void set_autocorrect_enabled(bool enabled)
```

Flips the user's "autocorrect misspelled words" setting (default true).

## check_count

```cpp
int check_count() const
```

How many times [check()](#check) ran, available or not, so a test can show a control didn't check again.

## generation

```cpp
std::uint64_t generation() const override
```

Starts at 1 and bumps on every change of the checker's state.

## check

```cpp
std::vector<SpellingError> check(std::string_view text) override
```

Reports each declared misspelling (SpellingAction::Suggest) or autocorrection (SpellingAction::Replace) in `text`, as byte offsets; added or ignored words are skipped. Words are runs of letters, digits, underscores and apostrophes, matched with exact case. This doesn't reproduce how the system checker splits words.

## suggest

```cpp
std::vector<std::string> suggest(std::string_view word) override
```

The suggestions declared with [add_misspelling()](#add_misspelling) for `word`, or empty.

## add_to_dictionary

```cpp
void add_to_dictionary(std::string_view word) override
```

Accepts `word` from now on and records it in [added()](#added).

## ignore_for_session

```cpp
void ignore_for_session(std::string_view word) override
```

Accepts `word` from now on and records it in [ignored()](#ignored).

## add_autocorrection

```cpp
void add_autocorrection(std::string_view from, std::string_view to) override
```

Makes [check()](#check) report `from` as a Replace error carrying `to`; wins over a misspelling.
